about: Checklist per brief, written on 11 November 2026 before any run's output was read. kind: 'state' = a screen or state a complete design of this journey has; 'info' = information the screens should carry (basis given). An item counts as present only if it is visible in the rendered text of at least one screen of the prototype. None of these items is stated in the brief. 'in_factory' says whether the Design Factory's knowledge files mention the item (all were written by the same author; see README, Limits).

D1.item: A name-check result that tells the customer the account is in a different or similar name and shows the actual account name 'D Kowalczyk Building Ltd' before the payment is made
A distinct state for a name that does not match at all (no match), with a warning
A state for when the name could not be checked (check unavailable)
A review screen before sending that repeats payee, account details, amount and reference together
A step where the customer approves the payment or confirms it is them (passcode, biometrics or similar, simulated)
A result screen for the payment being sent that includes the amount and the payee
A state for an amount over the £1,000 new-payee limit or over the available balance, saying what to do
D1.basis: brief fixture (limit) not turned into a state by the brief

D1.item: A state for the payment failing, being declined, or its outcome being unknown (for example a lost connection), saying whether money has left the account
Input validation errors on the payee or amount form that say how to fix the problem
A scam or fraud warning relevant to paying someone new (for example checking the payee is genuine, or that money may not be recoverable)
When the payment will arrive (for example 'usually within 2 hours' or 'within minutes')
A way to get help from the bank or to stop and contact the bank during the journey

D2.item: A summary box (a table or list of standard questions about the account, including 'What is the interest rate?' and 'Can I withdraw money?' or close equivalents) shown before the account is opened
An explanation of what AER means, or of the difference between AER and gross
A statement that the rate is variable and can change (beyond the single word 'variable' in the rate line), or how the customer will be told of changes
D2.basis: summary box: can the bank change the rate

D2.item: FSCS deposit protection mentioned with a limit
A way to get help from a person during the journey (a help link, chat or phone)
An example of interest in pounds (for example the balance after 12 months on £1,000, or interest on her £500)
The right to change her mind or cancel within 14 days
A step where the customer explicitly agrees to terms that are available to read (not pre-ticked)
A review screen before opening that repeats the account, the amount and where the money comes from
A result screen showing the account is open with £500.00 in it and what happens next (for example when interest is first paid)
Validation of the opening amount (below £1, above the available balance or above the maximum) with a message saying how to fix it
A state for the opening or the transfer failing, saying what happened to the money

D3.item: A plain statement that an overdraft is borrowing or a form of credit (debt), or that it is for short-term borrowing
The cost shown in pounds for an example (an amount borrowed for a number of days), or a cost calculator
A statement about the effect on her credit file or score (an eligibility check that does not affect it, or a warning that applying will be recorded)
The lower offer of £350 presented clearly as less than the £500 asked for, with accepting and declining both available
A declined state that is its own screen
D3.basis: brief says some customers are declined

D3.item: On being declined: that credit reference agency information was used, or that she can ask for the reason or a review
Help for money worries: the bank's support and/or free independent debt advice (for example MoneyHelper, StepChange, Citizens Advice)
The right to withdraw within 14 days, or how to reduce or remove the overdraft later
A step where she explicitly agrees to the overdraft agreement, with the agreement or pre-contract information available to read
Why income and outgoings are asked for (affordability)
A result screen for the accepted overdraft stating the limit, the rate and when it is available

D4.item: A way to freeze the card temporarily (reversible), separate from cancelling it
The frozen state shown in words, with a way to unfreeze
A question or choice that separates lost from stolen (or 'someone has used it')
A statement before confirming that cancelling the card is permanent or cannot be undone
A way to mark the NVX*DIGITAL payment as not recognised and report it
What happens next with the unrecognised payment (the bank will look into it or refund it, and when or how she will hear)
Confirmation of the delivery address for the replacement, with a way to say it is wrong
What still works or stops working while the card is frozen or cancelled (for example Direct Debits, digital wallet, subscriptions needing new details)
A result screen stating the card is cancelled and the replacement arrives in 3 to 5 working days
A phone number or other route to a person (for example the fraud team) in the journey
Security reassurance or advice (for example the bank will never ask for her PIN, or what to do about the PIN)
A state for the freeze, cancellation or order failing, saying what to do (for example call)

D5.item: A summary in words of total spending and the comparison with October (about £96 less)
Every category's amount shown as text next to or in its chart mark (not only in a legend or on hover)
The comparison says it is like for like (same point in last month), not the whole of October
The groceries budget shows spent (£212.35), the budget (£300.00) and what is left (£87.65)
The budget relates the money left to the time left in the month (for example 12 days left)
A category detail screen listing the six groceries payments with dates
A way to set a budget for a category that has none
A way to change or remove the existing budget
An over-budget state shown in words
An empty or loading state (for example a month or category with no spending, or data unavailable)
A way to correct a payment's category, or to see how categories are decided
Pending or incomplete data acknowledged (for example 'so far', 'up to 18 November', or pending payments noted)

D6.item: The Everyday balance labelled as 'available' balance (or the kind of balance stated)
The Tesco Express payment marked 'Pending' in words
An explanation of what pending means, on the home or the payment detail
The upcoming payments with a total (£1,099.50) or what will be left after them
Money in distinguished from money out by more than colour (a plus sign or words)
A payment detail screen with date, amount, payment method or type, and status
From the payment detail: a way to report a problem with the payment or get help
A loading state for the home screen
A state for balances or payments being unavailable (an error state that does not show £0.00 as a stand-in)
Payments grouped or labelled by day with dates
Quick actions (for example pay, move money, card, help) with text labels
